module.title: React Hooks And State Management
module.description: Learn how React manages dynamic behavior, state updates, side effects, and application logic using hooks.

lessons.title: What Are Hooks?

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Hooks are special React functions that allow components to use features like state and lifecycle behavior.

sections.heading: Why Hooks Exist
sections.content: As React applications became larger, managing logic inside components became difficult. Hooks simplified this process.

sections.heading: Hooks Add Power To Components
sections.content: Hooks allow components to store data, react to changes, fetch APIs, and handle application logic.

sections.heading: Modern React Depends On Hooks
sections.content: Most modern React applications use hooks instead of older class-based systems.

sections.heading: Hooks Improve Code Organization
sections.content: Hooks help developers separate logic into clean and reusable parts.

easyExample.title: Toolbox Example
easyExample.content: Hooks are like tools inside a toolbox. Each tool helps solve a specific problem inside the application.

summary: Hooks add advanced features to components

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: useState allows React components to store and update changing data.

sections.heading: Why State Matters
sections.content: Applications constantly change data like counters, forms, themes, notifications, and dashboards.

sections.heading: Dynamic Applications Need State
sections.content: Without state, applications could not update automatically when data changes.

sections.heading: How useState Works
sections.content: useState creates a variable and a function to update that variable.

sections.heading: React Automatically Updates UI
sections.content: Whenever state changes, React refreshes the UI automatically.

easyExample.title: Light Switch Example
easyExample.content: A light switch changes room brightness instantly. State changes update application UI similarly.

lessons.title: Understanding useEffect

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: useEffect runs code automatically when components load or data changes.

sections.heading: Why useEffect Exists
sections.content: Applications often need automatic actions like API calls, timers, authentication checks, or event listeners.

sections.heading: Running Side Effects
sections.content: useEffect handles operations happening outside normal UI rendering.

sections.heading: Component Lifecycle
sections.content: useEffect can run when components load, update, or disappear.

sections.heading: Real World Usage
sections.content: Fetching user data, checking login status, and loading dashboards commonly use useEffect.

easyExample.title: Automatic Fan Example
easyExample.content: A smart fan automatically starts when temperature changes. useEffect reacts automatically to changes similarly.

summary: Modern React apps use useEffect frequently

lessons.title: Forms And Controlled Components

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Controlled components are form inputs managed using React state.

sections.heading: Why Form State Matters
sections.content: Applications need to track user input dynamically while users type.

sections.heading: React Controls Input
sections.content: React stores input values inside state variables.

sections.heading: Dynamic Form Updates
sections.content: Whenever users type, state updates automatically.

sections.heading: Real Applications Depend On Form State
sections.content: Login forms, signup pages, search bars, and settings panels use controlled inputs.

easyExample.title: Notebook Example
easyExample.content: Imagine copying everything someone writes into a notebook instantly. React state tracks input similarly.

summary: Modern forms depend on state management

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Components go through different stages while running inside applications.

sections.heading: Component Creation
sections.content: A component first loads into the application interface.

sections.heading: Component Updates
sections.content: Whenever state or props change, React updates the component.

sections.heading: Component Removal
sections.content: Components can disappear when users navigate away or close sections.

sections.heading: Why Lifecycle Matters
sections.content: Applications need to manage timers, API requests, and cleanup operations correctly.

easyExample.title: Employee Shift Example
easyExample.content: Employees start work, perform tasks, and leave after shifts. Components follow similar stages.

lessons.title: State Management Thinking

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: State management controls how data moves and updates across applications.

sections.heading: Why State Management Matters
sections.content: Large applications contain many components needing shared data.

sections.heading: Local State vs Global State
sections.content: Some data belongs to one component while other data must be shared across the entire application.

sections.heading: Applications Depend On Shared Data
sections.content: Authentication, shopping carts, notifications, and themes often require shared state.

sections.heading: Scaling React Applications
sections.content: Proper state management keeps applications organized and maintainable.

easyExample.title: School Notice Board Example
easyExample.content: A school notice board shares important information with everyone. Global state works similarly inside applications.

summary: Applications depend on organized data flow
React scales using proper state management
